item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
item.description: In an interview with The Times, Meta’s chief executive took aim at Anthropic and OpenAI, which have pushed to tightly control A.I. development, and said he supported “more openness.”
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac and Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, said there needed to be people “bringing realism” to a debate about the way forward on artificial intelligence development.

item.title: OpenAI Close to Landing $500 Billion Data Center With Backing From Nvidia
item.description: The chipmaking giant is in talks with OpenAI to provide a $250 billion financial backstop for the project, which would be among the largest of the A.I. boom.
item.dc:creator: Maureen Farrell and Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Brian Kaiser/Bloomberg
item.media:description: The groundbreaking ceremony for the data center in Piketon, Ohio, in March. The financing for the project is indicative of the elaborate deals that have helped fuel the A.I. boom.

item.title: Apple Regains Spot Over Nvidia as Most Valuable Public Company
item.description: The company slipped by the chipmaker Nvidia, amid growing concern about costs associated with the artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Unlike the rest of the technology industry, Apple is not overhauling itself around AI.

item.title: Microsoft Unveils A.I. Cybersecurity Tools
item.description: As some executives fret over the safety of new A.I. systems, protecting against them could be a big business for tech companies.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz and Karen Weise
item.media:credit: Chona Kasinger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mustafa Suleyman, who oversees development of Microsoft’s A.I. models, says his company has deep knowledge of cybersecurity because its technology has faced so many attacks.

item.title: Nvidia Forms Alliance to Back Open-Source A.I. Amid Debate Over Safety
item.description: The company is continuing to back A.I. systems that can be freely used by others amid a continuing debate over the use of Chinese-made technology.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, has pushed for so-called open source A.I. that is built with his company’s computer chips.

item.title: Why Restarting a Nuclear Power Plant Can Be Much Harder Than Expected

item.title: Tesla Profit Falls Even as Car Sales Rebound

item.title: Lawsuit Against Meta Over Social Media Addiction Is Dropped
